title: Recipe mobile app with a GenAI cooking assistant
user_prompt: We're a small startup with a recipe app on iOS and Android. We have about 200,000 monthly active users, mostly in France, who open the app roughly 3 times a week. People browse recipes (lots of photos), save favourites, and upload photos of their own dishes. Last spring we added "Ask the chef", a chat feature where users ask cooking questions and get answers from an LLM; we use OpenAI for that and about a quarter of our users try it each month, with 2 or 3 questions per session. Our backend is on a cloud provider in Europe, I think it's a classic API plus a Postgres database and an object store for the photos. We'd like to understand the footprint of the app, and in particular what the AI feature changes.

facts_if_asked.backend: One Node API service, one managed Postgres, S3-compatible object storage for photos. No CDN.
facts_if_asked.photos: Average uploaded photo 2 MB after compression; recipe pages show about 6 thumbnails of 80 kB each.

expected_properties: A browsing journey and an 'Ask the chef' journey (or steps) that are distinguishable, so the AI feature's share can be read.
A GenAI API object with provider openai and a job on it, referenced from the chat step.
One API server and one database server shared across journeys; no duplicate database per journey.
Photo upload modeled as a job with significant data_transferred and data_stored, on the API or object store server.

Usage patterns on smartphone, mobile or wifi network, country FRANCE, with a volume consistent with 200k MAU x ~12 sessions/month (~2.4M journeys/month) or an explicit split between browsing and chat journeys.
open_questions should ask about things that matter: photo size/retention, model used, session mix.
